standard: Maintained experiments must make design provenance, bounded acceptance criteria, outcome, reproducibility, and exact revision-bound evidence explicit.

entries.question: Can Overcenter claim real work and deliver a self-contained byte-complete assignment to an empty disposable worker?
entries.claim: For the bounded proof workload, the claimed Work snapshot plus exact task bytes is sufficient for a no-checkout, no-network worker to produce candidate output that trusted authority can independently settle.
entries.contrast: Assign exact identity but require the worker to obtain source/input bytes through an ambient checkout or mount.
environment: Node.js from .node-version for the deterministic contract.
GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04 for the no-checkout worker and isolated network namespace.
success_criteria: A production SQLite kernel derives READY work and claims it at an exact revision.
The worker receives the claimed Work snapshot and all task-specific bytes in one immutable capsule.
The worker executes with no checkout, repository permission, execution capability, or outbound network namespace.
Missing or altered required bytes fail closed before execution.
Candidate bytes bind to the exact assignment digest, obligation, run, and claimed revision.
Trusted reconstruction and independent observation settle the same run DONE.

artifacts: GitHub Actions run 35488740731: exact-head hosted assignment capsule proof; deterministic contract, no-checkout worker, isolated network namespace, damaged-assignment controls, and trusted settlement all passed.

entries.interpretation: A positive result proves byte-complete assignment plumbing for the bounded workload; it does not make the worker authoritative for success or imply arbitrary toolchain portability.
non_claims: The Node runtime or Linux kernel are embedded in the assignment.
This is a general artifact distribution or confidential payload service.
Arbitrary provider mutation is authorized by the worker capsule.
Every future obligation already fits this proof packet.

design.note: The boundary and fail-closed criteria were committed on the experiment branch before the hosted proof result; later exact-head runs confirm the same bounded contract.

outcome.summary: Exact claimed work and task bytes were delivered to a no-checkout, no-network worker and independently settled by trusted authority.

entries.question: Can ClaimFact, ExecutionAuthorityFact, and EffectReservationFact safely collapse to Claim + Attempt while actually reducing machinery and preserving performance?
entries.claim: In the bounded recovery model, one Attempt clock cannot simultaneously rotate to fence stale workers and remain stable to represent an unresolved external mutation. A safe Claim + Attempt representation therefore recreates the missing dimension as execute/recover purpose plus unresolved-effect identity, preserving safety and throughput but not reducing writes or source surface.
entries.contrast: Keep semantic claim ownership, execution/recovery fencing, and unresolved external-effect reservation as distinct state dimensions.

design.note: The simplification hypothesis and acceptance thresholds were fixed before hosted confirmation, while the candidate shape was informed by prior production-code inspection and exploratory local modeling.

outcome.summary: The safe collapse preserved safety and met the performance bound but grew the bounded authority model from 88 to 107 SLOC (+21.6%) with unchanged representative durable-write counts. Both smaller single-clock variants fail: rotating the clock admits a successor while the prior external mutation remains unresolved; preserving it fails to fence stale authority.

environment: Node.js from .node-version for the executable differential.
Pinned Lean semantic oracle revision 39bd16a317bc2155a17b6674a5050adaf4295c90 for the universal two-clock necessity theorem.
No provider credential, database, or model is required for the deterministic experiment.
success_criteria: The safe candidate rejects stale authority after recovery fencing.
Recovery-only authority cannot execute a second unresolved external effect.
Replay-safe computation still requires proof that the prior containment domain terminated.
Representative durable-write counts are no worse than the legacy-shaped reference.
The safe candidate is smaller than the legacy-shaped reference by at least 5% SLOC for the proposed simplification to be supported.
If one Attempt clock rotates on recovery, the negative control demonstrates duplicate external-effect eligibility unless unresolved-effect state is tracked separately.
If one Attempt clock is preserved across recovery to retain mutation identity, the negative control demonstrates that stale execution authority remains accepted.
Median in-process effect-recovery transition time remains within 1.25x of the legacy-shaped reference over seven 200,000-transaction samples.
The pinned Lean oracle proves for arbitrary epoch types that authority rotation plus mutation-epoch persistence contradicts a single clock that remains aliased before and after recovery.

authority-model-sloc: legacy 88, safe candidate 107, unsafe candidate 33
effect-recovery-throughput: 200000 iterations, legacy median 20.043804 ms, candidate median 15.031002 ms, ratio 0.749908
TLA+ transition kernel and resource-containment negative controls behaved as expected in run 35757238433
Production Rust worker confinement boundary PASS in run 35757238433
Pinned Lean oracle 39bd16a317bc2155a17b6674a5050adaf4295c90: single_clock_recovery_impossible and recovery_requires_distinct_clock_dimension

entries.interpretation: The negative result is about temporal factorization, not naming: claim lifetime, authority epoch, and mutation-uncertainty lifetime are not coextensive. A safe simplification must preserve those dimensions while reducing surrounding choreography rather than aliasing them into one clock.
non_claims: The in-process transition benchmark represents provider I/O, SQLite latency, or native executor overhead.
The Go computation executor should be retained or removed.
The present production implementation is globally minimal.
No alternative representation can reduce code while preserving the same independent temporal dimensions.

entries.interpretation: Multiple READY nodes are not themselves an AI prioritization problem. The controlling difficulty is the size and overlap of the remaining interacting objective kernel, not raw graph size. Exceeding a deterministic budget still calls first for stronger deterministic optimization or decomposition, not automatic AI escalation. Changing receipt run identity changes the existing SQLite-style outer commit digest, demonstrating that the authority spine still binds per-run identity without a second Merkle execution object.
Missing evidence cannot project DONE, and no false DONE occurs.

128 receipt-v5 facts were generated through the production kernel/effect adapter, read back through validated SqliteFactStore.history, hydrated from evidence references, and replayed with 0 semantic mismatches and 0 false DONE outcomes.

The 128-receipt corpus stored exactly one shared evidence object; evidence tamper and missing-evidence controls were rejected, and changing run identity changed the SQLite-style outer commit digest.

entries.interpretation: The evidence favors a smaller architecture than a second receipt DAG. Overcenter's SQLite/Git fact history already supplies the authoritative content-addressed outer spine; reusable certified observations and future execution-trace payloads can be content-addressed leaves referenced by ordinary settlement facts. This preserves existing settlement authority and exact run/revision binding while gaining tamper detection, deduplication, and independently retrievable evidence.
non_claims: Every observation is safe to deduplicate merely because its bytes match; verifier/subject/snapshot provenance remains part of the evidence bytes.
The production SQLite schema should be changed on the strength of this single corpus.
Canonical JSON bytes equal physical SQLite or object-store bytes.
Commit-level content addressing replaces authoritative observation or current-realization admissibility.
Evidence leaves provide process/syscall/network record-replay.
Backend-local authority identities become portable across SQLite and Git.

design.note: The leaf-only architecture, authoritative-history readback requirement, 128-receipt corpus, <=0.56x storage threshold, tamper/missing controls, and outer-commit identity control were fixed before the first hosted run.

outcome.summary: At exact revision 1ad6c4f97d698f3e194b5e8ec74bf4050084bf14, the leaf-only treatment preserved exact receipt-v5/projectReceipt semantics with zero false DONE, used one shared evidence object, and reached 0.302x flat bytes at 128 receipts. On the same hosted run, the fuller receipt DAG used 0.506x, so retaining the existing authority spine and Merkleizing only repeated evidence was both simpler and materially smaller for this corpus.

entries.question: Across realistic replay-evidence sizes and reuse rates, when does content-addressed evidence externalization beat inline receipt storage, and what recovery/GC costs does that indirection introduce?
entries.claim: Evidence CAS is not a universal storage win: zero-reuse evidence will remain larger than inline storage, while increasing payload size and reuse will produce measurable crossover curves. A deterministic group-cost policy that externalizes only when refs plus one stored object are smaller than repeated inline payloads will never exceed flat canonical bytes across the preregistered matrix and will preserve exact receipt-v5 semantics.
entries.contrast: Always externalize every evidence payload into CAS regardless of size or reuse, or always keep all evidence inline.
environment: Node.js from .node-version on Linux x86-64 for the hosted run.
A corpus of 128 actual production GitHub receipt-v5 identities is generated once through OvercenterKernel and performGithubCommitStatusEffect.
Execution-trace diagnostics are schema-valid non-semantic receipt-v5 data layered onto those production identities, validated by validateReceiptFact and replayed through production projectReceipt.
Trace payload sizes are 1 KiB, 16 KiB, 256 KiB, and 1 MiB; reuse fractions are 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% with deterministic exact-byte traces.

Logical storage accounting uses canonical JSON bytes for inline receipts, reference receipts, and unique CAS objects. File-system lookup and GC measurements use a temporary local directory CAS on the hosted runner.
Physical database pages, remote object-store billing, compression, and network RTT are outside this experiment.
success_criteria: Every hydrated externalized receipt is canonically identical to its inline receipt-v5 fact and production projectReceipt preserves disposition and verified result with zero false DONE.
Universal externalization is larger than inline storage at 0% reuse for every preregistered payload size, establishing the no-reuse negative control.
At 100% reuse, universal externalization is smaller than inline storage for every preregistered payload size.
The experiment reports universal CAS byte ratios for every payload-size/reuse cell and the first measured reuse crossover for each payload size.

A deterministic exact-cost policy that externalizes a digest group only when reference receipts plus one CAS object are smaller than that group's inline receipts never exceeds flat canonical bytes in any matrix cell.
For a 256 KiB, 50%-reuse representative corpus, file-backed CAS lookup verifies the requested digest on every read and reports p50/p95 lookup latency.
A mark-and-sweep GC control over the representative corpus deletes all injected orphan objects, deletes no live object, and reports reclaimed bytes and sweep latency.
Cold recovery bandwidth for the representative corpus is reported as reference bytes plus unique evidence bytes; warm recovery bandwidth after evidence caching is reported as reference bytes only.

artifacts: GitHub Actions run 35823476017, job 107060113122: evidence CAS break-even matrix PASS.
All 20 payload/reuse cells preserved receipt-v5/projectReceipt semantics with 0 semantic mismatches and 0 false DONE.
Universal CAS ratios at 0% reuse were >1 for every payload: 1.0167x (1 KiB), 1.0029x (16 KiB), 1.0002x (256 KiB), 1.0001x (1 MiB).
The first sampled universal-CAS crossover was 25% reuse for every payload size. At 50% reuse ratios were 0.8498x, 0.5608x, 0.5043x, and 0.5011x as payload size increased.
The exact-cost selective policy never exceeded flat bytes; at 0% reuse it externalized zero groups, and at 25% reuse it externalized only the 32 repeated groups while leaving singleton groups inline.

Representative 256 KiB / 50%-reuse file CAS: verified lookup p50 2429.117 us, p95 5060.002 us; cold recovery 17,063,250 bytes vs 33,837,074 flat; warm recovery 282,514 bytes; GC deleted 16/16 orphans, reclaimed 4,195,184 bytes, and took 718.197 us.

entries.interpretation: Evidence CAS should be infrastructure, not a mandatory receipt representation. The dominant decision variable in this matrix is whether exact evidence bytes repeat; payload size mainly controls how large the win becomes. A deterministic cost comparison per digest group avoids a guessed global threshold: keep singleton evidence inline when externalization is more expensive, and externalize repeated evidence when one CAS object plus references is smaller. Large unique traces may still merit CAS for operational reasons, but that is not a storage optimization and should be justified separately.
non_claims: The matrix represents the empirical distribution of production Overcenter replay traces.
Local filesystem latency predicts remote object-store latency.
Canonical-byte savings equal physical SQLite, Git, compressed object-store, or network billing savings.
Repeated evidence is semantically reusable unless its complete provenance-bearing bytes are identical.
GC of evidence objects is safe without tracing all authoritative receipt references.
Evidence CAS replaces authoritative observation, settlement authority, or current-realization checks.

design.note: Payload sizes, reuse fractions, 128-receipt corpus, zero-reuse and full-reuse controls, exact-cost selective policy, representative lookup/GC case, and reported recovery bandwidth metrics were fixed before the first hosted run.

outcome.summary: At exact revision 9bf7dc83d36700c022dcbf1af2a77ff873809cb2, universal evidence CAS was confirmed to be a small storage loss at zero reuse and a substantial win once evidence repeated. Across the preregistered matrix, the first sampled universal crossover was 25% reuse for every payload size, while the exact-cost selective policy never exceeded flat storage because it kept singleton groups inline. The 256 KiB/50%-reuse file-backed control halved cold recovery bytes, reduced warm recovery to reference-only bytes, verified every lookup digest, and swept all injected orphans without deleting live evidence.
